sentences.text: By way of preferring the present application under Section 482 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973, the present applicant (i.e. the original accused no.7) seeks to invoke the inherent powers of this Court, praying to quash and set-aside the First Information Report No.11208001220123 of 2022 lodged before the Mahila Police Station, Rajkot city, for the offences punishable under Sections 498A, 504 and 114 of the Indian Penal Code.
4. The present applicant, who is the sister-in-law ('derani') of the complainant, has been arraigned as accused no.7 in the FIR.

Learned advocate Ms.Maitri P.Patel appearing for the applicant, at the outset, has submitted that a Coordinate Bench of this Court, vide order dated 06.03.2024, has stayed the proceedings of the impugned FIR against the present applicant.

Learned advocate Ms.Patel has further submitted that after the investigation, NEUTRAL CITATION R/CR.MA/23945/2022 JUDGMENT DATED: 27/02/2026 undefined the police had filed the charge-sheet against the other co- accused, who are not before this Court.

She has also submitted that during the pendency of the trial, settlement took place between the parties, and the complainant, in her evidence at Exh.22, has specifically stated before the trial court that due to trivial household chores, she had to file the impugned FIR.

It is submitted that since the complainant did not support the case of the prosecution and turned hostile, the learned 10th Additional Chief Judicial Magistrate, Rajkot, vide judgment and order dated 18.03.2024 passed below application Exh.27 in Criminal Case No.28337 of 2022, acquitted all the accused persons except the present applicant, and while acquitting the other co-accused, the trial court directed the Investigating Officer to file a separate supplementary charge-sheet against the present applicant,
which is improper and illegal considering the fact that the Coordinate Bench has already stayed the proceedings qua the present applicant.
5. Learned advocate Ms.Patel, while traversing the factual NEUTRAL CITATION R/CR.MA/23945/2022 JUDGMENT DATED: 27/02/2026 undefined matrix of the case, has submitted that the trial court has already acquitted all co-accused, including the husband and in-laws of the complainant.

While referring to the judgment and order of the trial court, learned advocate Ms.Patel has submitted that it appears from the said judgment that the trial court, after considering the fact that the complainant did not support the case of the prosecution and turned hostile attributing the dispute to trivial household chores, acquitted all co-accused except the present applicant- accused.
Furthermore, she has submitted that there is not an iota of evidence to implicate the present applicant in the alleged offence.

6. Learned advocate Ms.Patel has submitted that the complainant has made general allegations against the applicant-accused, and the FIR, even if it is considered at its face value, the same could not even establish the offence as alleged in the FIR.
She has, therefore, urged that considering the above, the application may be allowed and the impugned FIR may be quashed and set-aside.
NEUTRAL CITATION R/CR.MA/23945/2022 JUDGMENT DATED: 27/02/2026 undefined 7.

While vehemently opposing the present application, learned APP Mr.Manan Maheta appearing for the respondent - State has submitted that considering the allegations levelled against the present applicant, this Court may not entertain the present application and the same may be rejected.

sentences.text: Having gone through the materials on record including the judgment of the trial court as well as having considered the arguments canvassed by learned advocates for the respective parties, it appears that the complainant had filed the impugned complaint against her husband and in-laws including the present applicant on trivial household chores, and later on, the matter was settled.

Therefore, it prima facie appears that the trial court, after having considered the fact that the complainant did not support the case of the prosecution and turned hostile, acquitted all other accused persons including her husband and in-laws except the present applicant-accused vide judgment and order dated NEUTRAL CITATION R/CR.MA/23945/2022 JUDGMENT DATED:
27/02/2026 undefined 18.03.2024 passed below application Exh.27 in Criminal Case No.28337 of 2022.

9. Be that as it may, this Court has also considered the allegations made by the complainant against the present applicant-accused in the FIR, which clearly appear to be vague, omnibus and general in nature.

Furthermore, it appears from the judgment and order of the trial court that while acquitting the other co-accused including the husband and in-laws of the complainant, it directed the Investigating Officer to file a separate supplementary charge-sheet against the present applicant,
which is improper and illegal in view of the fact that the Coordinate Bench has already stayed the proceedings qua the present applicant.

It is noteworthy that when the trial court itself has acquitted the main accused persons (i.e. the husband and other in-laws), then there is no point in continuing further with the criminal proceedings against the present applicant-accused, who is the sister-in-law ('derani') of the complainant, when the complainant herself has deposed NEUTRAL CITATION R/CR.MA/23945/2022 JUDGMENT DATED: 27/02/2026 undefined before the trial court that on account of trivial household chores she had to file the impugned FIR, and later on, the matter was settled and she turned hostile.

10. This Court is quite conscious of the fact that the power under Section 482 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973, is extraordinary power, and it should be used sparingly, as the exercise of such power would scuttle the FIR at the threshold.
But, if the FIR fails to make out essential ingredients of the offence, the power should be exercised.
Upshot of the above discussion, the present application deserves consideration.
11. In the result, the present application is allowed.

The First Information Report No.11208001220123 of 2022 lodged before the Mahila Police Station, Rajkot city, for the offences punishable under Sections 498A, 504 and 114 of the Indian Penal Code, is hereby ordered to be quashed and set-aside.
All consequential proceedings arising pursuant thereto are also quashed and set-aside.
NEUTRAL CITATION R/CR.MA/23945/2022 JUDGMENT DATED: 27/02/2026 undefined 12.
Rule made absolute.
Direct service is permitted.

(VIMAL K. VYAS, J.) /MOINUDDIN Reenaben Vipul Patar vs State Of Gujarat on 27 February, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/61342106/
